Watch for the turning point, then we'll begin the early, drastic heat cuts well before RoR misbehaves as we approach Maillard/first crack. No drop in drying.

Pre-FC at 146C, ~5:20 in, running heat pinned at 100% with low fan 30%. Bean RoR is only ~9.6 C/min and easing — but with full heat still applied and thermal lag, energy is banked and we risk a late RoR spike or scorched/baked flavor from too little convection. Cut heat decisively to 75% now (ahead of the lag) and lift fan to 40% to shift toward convective transfer, even out the bean pile, and evacuate smoke/chaff. This sets up a smooth RoR decline into first crack rather than a flatten or flick-up. Hold for the next minute and reassess as we approach FC.

Just 15s into development (~2.7% ratio); need to reach ~15% near 83s of development. Bean is 184C with RoR ~10C/min, still on full heat at 100% — that will run away past target before development matures. Cut heat decisively to 75 and lift fan to 45 to shift toward convective transfer, evacuate smoke, and ease RoR so development stretches without darkening too fast. Hold; reassess as ratio builds toward target.

Development is only ~45s into a ~587s roast, a ratio of ~7.7% — well short of the 15% target, so keep going. Post-crack bean RoR is still ~11 C/min, too hot to stretch development cleanly. Cut heat to 45 and raise fan to 70 to shift toward convective transfer, ease the RoR, and protect flavor. At 189 C you have room to develop toward and modestly past the 197 C guide while building duration. Reassess for drop as the ratio approaches ~12-15%.

Drum is at 186 C, already inside the 180-200 C charge band, but heat is pinned at 100% and bean temp is still climbing ~19 C/min — left alone it will overshoot the band. Cut heat decisively to ~60% now (thermal lag means the current rise will continue for a bit) to arrest the climb and let it settle near the band midpoint. Nudge fan to 15 for a touch more convective evenness and to evacuate any chaff. Not ready to charge this second — hold ~30-60s for the temperature to stabilize, then charge once it's steady around 190-195 C.

At ~5:12, bean temp 141C climbing toward first crack with heat pinned at 100% and fan at only 10%. That's a lot of stored energy in the element with minimal convective transfer — classic setup for an RoR spike into FC and scorched/baked flavor. Cut heat decisively now to anticipate thermal lag (a trim won't bite in time), and raise fan to shift toward convective heat for even roasting and to start evacuating chaff/smoke. RoR is currently a healthy ~11 C/min and easing; this keeps the decline smooth into first crack without stalling. Not dropping — pre-FC.

First crack just hit (2.5s in, ratio ~0.5%) — far from the 16.2% target. Heat is pinned at 100% with post-crack RoR still ~9 C/min, which would race through development. Cut heat decisively to 70% to tame the rise and raise fan to 45 for convective evenness and smoke/chaff evacuation, stretching development. Hold; reassess as bean temp approaches the 193 C guide and the ratio builds toward target.

Development is only ~64s (10.7% ratio) vs 16.2% target, so keep developing. Bean RoR has eased nicely to ~8.8 C/min at 187 C — already cut hard to 30%. Hold heat low (35%) with fan at 70% to sustain convective transfer and a gentle climb without spiking RoR. Aim to drop around 90-100s development (~16%), likely near 191-193 C. Not yet.
